en: According to the *Dunhuang Records*, Guocheng was originally a fishing marsh. During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Han dynasty, Cui Buyi taught people how to cultivate the land and obtain grain;
it was named accordingly and later became a county. Ershi Spring is located three stages east of Shacheng.
During the Han dynasty, when General Li Guangli’s army was suffering from thirst and exhaustion during a march,
he prayed to the mountain deity and pierced the mountain with his sword;
consequently, water flowed forth.
Flowing westward for several tens of *li*, it reaches Huangzhang Bo.
Later there was a general who,
being extremely thirsty, drank from its water.
The spring ceased at its side,
and the water subsequently stopped flowing;
it reached only as far as level ground.
Later, if there are many people, the water is abundant;
if there are few people, the water is scarce.
If the multitude of the district drinks the water greedily, it will descend with great force.
It remains so to this day.
The temples of these two masters stand by the roadside,
having long been abandoned.
There is merely a mound of piled stones,
a place where camels, horses, and travelers come to pray for blessings.
Continuing eastward, one enters the borders of Guazhou.
To the south of the prefecture lies the Mogao Caves,
twenty-five *li* from the city. On the way there,
one must cross a rocky desert.
Carrying the mountain slopes to that place,
it descends into the valley;
to its east is Mount Sanwei.
To the west is Mount Mingsha;
from within it flows a stream from the south known as the Dangquan.
The monastic quarters of the ancient temple are extremely numerous,
and there is also a large bronze bell.
At both the northern and southern ends of the valley, there are shrines for the Heavenly Kings and local deities.
The murals depict the retinue of the Tibetan *btsan-po*.
To the west of that mountain, the cliff extends two *li* from north to south;
it is entirely composed of high and large sandstone caves carved out by excavation.
The Buddha images are fashioned from clay and painted;
the cost for each cave typically amounts to several million taels.
In front of each, multi-storied pavilions have been constructed.
There is a great hall for a colossal image;
the image is one hundred and sixty feet tall,
and there are countless smaller niches.
Throughout, there are empty railings and passages,
forming a continuous circuit for the sites of pilgrimage and sightseeing.
Next, on the southern mountain, is the place where Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared.
Whenever the people of the commandery went to visit him,
they invariably traveled on foot;
such was their reverence.
Mingsha Mountain is ten *li* from the prefectural seat.
The mountain extends eighty *li* from east to west and forty *li* from south to north.
It rises five hundred feet high and is composed entirely of a mound of sand;
this mountain possesses supernatural wonders.
The peaks are as if carved from stone;
within them lies a well that sand cannot cover.
It resounds spontaneously during the height of summer;
when people and horses tread upon it, its sound vibrates for several tens of li.
Regarding local custom, on the day of the Duanwu Festival:
The children within the city all climbed to the high peak and leaped down together;
the sound of the sand crashing was like the roar of thunder.
When he went to look at it at dawn,
the steep cliffs remained as they were before.
This place was anciently known as Mingsha (Singing Sands).
They deified the sand and established a shrine there.
To the south is a sweet spring that flows from the southern side of Sand Mountain.
Its source originates in the Great Snow Mountains;
it enters Dunhuang from the southwest across the border of Shouchang County.
Because of its power to provide fertility and moisture, it is popularly known as "Sweet Spring" (Ganquan).
Mount Kimsan is located to the southwest of Mount Sasan.
It always has snow during the summer months.
Within the mountain is a shrine dedicated to a deity.
It is extremely efficacious;
people dare not approach it.
Every year, the local deity offers a fine horse as a sacrifice during the ritual of gazing upon the shrine.
They were driven into the mountains;
as they drew near, there immediately arose calamities of thunder, lightning, wind, and hail.
To the southwest of the prefecture is a temple dedicated to King Li Xian.
This was the ancestral temple of the late King Zhao of Xiliang.
In the Qianfeng era,
an auspicious stone was discovered beside the temple.
Its color was a deep azure-green.
Upon it were red characters in an ancient script which read:
"The dynastic succession shall last for thirty generations."
It was prophesied that its years would last seven hundred.
Today, people call it the Temple of Li.
To the west of the prefecture is Yang Pass.
This was the old Yumen Pass.
Because Yang Mingzhao, the Regional Inspector of Shazhou, fled through this pass after being pursued for refusing his orders,
later generations called it the Yang Pass.
It borders the city of Shanshan;
the terrain is treacherous and lacks water and grass,
such that human passage is impossible.
The pass was later moved to the east of the prefecture.
Eighty-five *li* west of the city is the Jade Maiden Spring (*Yunüquan*).
Popular tradition claims there is some truth to this:
every year, this district conscripts one boy and one girl from among the children to serve as offerings to the deity of the pond.
If the harvest follows the seasons, it will be successful;
otherwise, the seedlings will be damaged.
Although parents suffer when separated from their children, [they must let them go].
She was recorded by the spirits;
joyfully taking hands with them, she passed away among the divine dragons.
When Prefect Zhang Xiaosong took office, he sought her out.
The people of the commandery informed him.
The Grand Governor said in anger,
"How can there be such a river-source demon harming my people?"
He then established an altar beside Xingquan Spring and said,
"I pray to behold your true form,
for I wish to offer sacrifice to you in person."
The deity then transformed into a dragon and emerged from the water;
the Governor struck its throat with his arrow and drew his sword to sever its head.
He presented it in person at the palace gate,
where Emperor Xuanzong praised it repeatedly.
He subsequently bestowed upon him a dragon-tongue sword.
The imperial edict bestowed upon it the name "Dragon Tongue.
It is recorded in the registers compiled by the Zhang family.
One *li* to the northwest of the prefectural city, there is a temple.
Ancient trees cast a dense shade.
Within them stands a small fortress,
upon which a corridor and hall are established.
This is specific and verifiable.
Previously, there was the District Magistrate Zhang Qiu,
who had already transcended the stage of "following the heart."
I have taken up residence here;
though not widely learned,
I have exerted myself with great earnestness.
For many years, the land had been in turmoil and those who practiced the study of the teachings were few;
consequently, he gathered together the younger generation.
By thus elucidating the Great Way,
Heaven did not neglect or abandon him;
the people received its bounty.
Gypsum Mountain is located two hundred and fifty-six *li* to the north of the prefecture.
Its name derives from the fact that gypsum exudes from the crevices between the rocks on Mount Wu and Mount Feng.
It was established in the nineteenth year of the Kaihuang era.
The black mountain turned white;
this central verification was not in vain. He dispatched seven Daoist practitioners, including Huangfu Decong, to perform sacrificial rites and incantations.
From here, Mount Wang (Wangshifeng) is visible;
it is located two hundred and thirty li northwest of Hexiang City.
In ancient times, military provisions were stored there.
The Great Wall is located to the north of the prefecture.
The wall extends for sixty-three *li* and enters the desert sands directly to the west.
Established by divination during the Former Han dynasty;
it enters the borders of Yizhou from the north.
